sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, Chapter 1
sources.locator: Complete HTML Chapter 1; §1.1.1, equations 1.6–1.15, real scalar action and Klein–Gordon variation.

contents.name: §1.1.1: normalized real scalar action and Euler–Lagrange equation

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §1.1.1 from the action definition through the computed derivatives and Klein–Gordon equation, including the stated +--- metric convention.
source_review.supports: The scalar quadratic density with coefficient one-half and its Euler–Lagrange Klein–Gordon equation.
source_review.limitations: Tong uses +---; the item fixes -+++ and redoes the variation with its own eta and Box definitions. The source supplies no Dirac-domain or empirical claim.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, Chapter 2
sources.locator: Complete HTML Chapter 2; §§2.2, 2.6.1, 2.7 and 2.7.1, including equations 2.123–2.127 and 2.164–2.174.

contents.name: §2.2: scalar Fock sectors, number operator and formal point-field warning

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete displayed Fock-sector and number-operator discussion and its following operator-valued-distribution caveat.
source_review.supports: The Fock-sector reading of the number operator and the warning that point fields are not ordinary Fock-space operators.
source_review.limitations: The source uses formal delta(0) notation. The item replaces that heuristic with the exact shell-norm divergence and current Fock domains.

contents.name: §2.7.1: time ordering of the free scalar two-point function

source_review.read_extent: Read the full §2.7.1 definition of the time-ordered two-point function, its positive and negative time branches, and the ensuing four-momentum representation discussion.
source_review.supports: The two branches are the ordered Wightman functions and the kernel has the Klein–Gordon Green-source normalization.
source_review.limitations: The source uses +--- and the standard Feynman prefactor-i convention. The carrier explicitly uses -+++, has no extra i, and proves the distributional extension directly.

contents.name: §2.7.1: derivative jump and Feynman Green equation

source_review.read_extent: Read equations 2.170–2.174 and the contour calculation yielding the time-ordered shell branches.
source_review.supports: The mode factor has a time-ordering jump that produces the Klein–Gordon delta source.
source_review.limitations: The example supplies its own half-line distributional integration-by-parts proof and fixes the local sign and prefactor conventions.

source_review.read_extent: Read equations 2.165–2.169 relating the free scalar vacuum two-point function to its time-ordered counterpart.
source_review.supports: The Wightman kernel and its exchange under reversing the two arguments.
source_review.limitations: The local item uses the actual QFT-MF02 draft Wightman statement and its exact second-variable-linear pairing.

sources.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes, Chapter 4
sources.locator: Complete HTML Chapter 4; §§4.2–4.3, equations 4.342–4.359, Dirac adjoint, action and Euler–Lagrange equations.

source_review.read_extent: Read §4.2 from the failure of psi-dagger psi through the Dirac adjoint and chosen action, then §4.3 through the independent psi and psi-bar variations and both equations.
source_review.supports: The Dirac action, adjoint convention, and the formal Euler–Lagrange equations.
source_review.limitations: Tong uses +--- and varies psi and psi-bar independently. The item fixes its own QFT-MF03 matrices and proves the equivalent real-variation statement for commuting classical spinors.

sources.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, complete author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft
sources.locator: Complete 616-page author-hosted draft; §3, equations 3.7–3.16; §8, equations 8.11–8.15; §36, equations 36.1–36.11.

contents.name: §3: real scalar action, compact-variation Euler–Lagrange equation and mass-shell normalization

source_review.read_extent: Read §3 from the adopted Klein–Gordon equation through the scalar action variation, integration by parts, shell equation and positive-frequency mass-shell density.
source_review.supports: The normalized quadratic scalar action and the classical Klein–Gordon equation.
source_review.limitations: The source uses +--- and hbar=c=1; the item states a mathematical inverse-length parameter and rederives the sign under -+++.

contents.name: §8: free scalar Feynman propagator and time-ordered vacuum two-point function

source_review.read_extent: Read §8 from the Gaussian generating functional and propagator definition through the shell formula, Green equation and two-point time-ordering identity.
source_review.supports: The free scalar propagator is the time-ordered two-point function and solves the Klein–Gordon Green equation.
source_review.limitations: The source uses a prefactor i and a formal momentum-space boundary prescription. The local carrier uses no prefactor i and supplies the full tempered-distribution proof.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §8 derivation of the shell time factor from the momentum-space pole prescription and the resulting Green normalization.
source_review.supports: The scalar mode has a first-derivative discontinuity at the time-ordering surface.
source_review.limitations: The local example computes the jump directly and does not rely on a contour or pole prescription.

contents.name: §36: spinor Lagrangian and equations of motion

source_review.read_extent: Read §36 from the Weyl-spinor Lagrangian construction and variation through the four-component Dirac action and equation; also inspected the stated anticommutation convention in §35.
source_review.supports: The spinor kinetic and mass terms and the Dirac equation obtained by variation.
source_review.limitations: Srednicki explicitly uses anticommuting spinor fields. The item uses commuting classical spinors and supplies its own complete real-variation argument; no Grassmann rule is imported.
